flux.description: Widen the flux manager past its gotk-only default. Renovate ships flux with managerFilePatterns of just `/(?:^|/)gotk-components\.ya?ml$/`, which finds the Flux distribution itself and nothing a consumer writes — so a `GitRepository.spec.ref.tag` (github-tags) or a Flux `Kustomization.spec.images` entry (docker) in a repo's own manifests is invisible until the pattern is widened. Keep the upstream pattern in the list: managerFilePatterns REPLACES the default rather than extending it, so dropping it would stop tracking gotk-components fleet-wide. Widening to `infrastructure/**` is safe against false positives because Renovate's flux schema validates apiVersion prefixes (`kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/`, `source.toolkit.fluxcd.io/`, `helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io/`): a plain kustomize `kustomization.yaml` is `kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1` and is skipped, so ordinary Kubernetes YAML under infrastructure/ yields no deps.

packageRules.description: Disable Renovate's built-in mise manager fleet-wide: consumer .mise.toml tool pins are TEMPLATE-OWNED (enforced by standards' normalize-mise-pins.sh against template/.mise.toml.jinja floors). Letting Renovate also bump .mise.toml created an infinite thrash (Renovate bumps up, copier-sync reverts to floor). Currency for these tools is driven from the template's .mise.toml.jinja via custom managers in the standards repo, so one reviewed bump propagates uniformly to the whole fleet. NOTE: does NOT affect the jdx/mise CLI pin below — that is a custom.regex manager (workflow YAML), a different manager.

Major updates are migrations, not background maintenance. Keep them visible in the Dependency Dashboard but do not create a branch, PR, or downstream CI run until an operator explicitly approves the update.
Pre-1.0 dependencies can break on any release, so require explicit Dependency Dashboard approval before Renovate creates their branch and triggers downstream CI.

Standing automerge for the safe classes: non-major updates (minor/patch/pin/digest/pinDigest) of stable >=1.0.0 deps, every manager, dev and runtime alike. Subsumes the previous devDependencies and github-actions/dockerfile rules. Majors and 0.x packages stay manual. platformAutomerge has been ON for this rule since 2026-08-03. GitHub-native auto-merge waits only on required checks, while Renovate's own engine waits for every check, so the original fleet had too few required contexts for a safe native handoff. The 2026-07-30 gate-tests rollout added the repo-owned required `test-gate` context for the 34 repos carrying `gate_tests=true`; `.github-private`#179 then closed the same-day lint/e2e gap by making `lint-hooks / lint-hooks` and `e2e / e2e` required through property-targeted org rulesets. The seven governed repos without test-gate carry zero language facets except playwright-skills, so their lack of a test context is not an unfixed rollout hole. platformAutomerge is safe here because the checks each consumer actually renders are required before GitHub merges.

Lockfile maintenance only refreshes transitive resolution inside existing ranges - the lowest-risk update class. minimumReleaseAge:0 is required for the automerge to ever fire: under the global 7-day soak, Renovate stamps its own `renovate/stability-days` pending status whenever any refreshed transitive release is younger than 7 days, its merge engine waits for ALL checks including that one, and the next weekly refresh pulls new young releases that re-arm the clock - so the PR stays green-but-unmergeable indefinitely (standards#404 sat 8 days; hand-merged 2026-08-03). The soak exists to vet just-published DIRECT updates; lockfile refreshes stay inside ranges already vetted by their own PRs.

Ungrouped stable npm minor and patch updates share one rolling PR while inheriting the standing safe automerge posture. The current-version guard keeps pre-1.0 packages out, and the JSONata guard preserves an earlier narrower monorepo group.
Ungrouped pre-1.0 npm minor and patch updates remain human-reviewed in a branch distinct from stable npm updates. The JSONata guard preserves an earlier narrower monorepo group.

Ungrouped stable Cargo minor and patch updates share one rolling PR while inheriting the standing safe automerge posture. The current-version guard keeps pre-1.0 crates out, and the JSONata guard preserves an earlier narrower monorepo group.
Ungrouped pre-1.0 Cargo minor and patch updates remain human-reviewed in a branch distinct from stable Cargo updates. The JSONata guard preserves an earlier narrower monorepo group.

Ungrouped stable dependency pin updates share a safe automerge branch without being blocked by a pre-1.0 pin. The JSONata guard preserves earlier narrower groups, and later package-specific grouping rules remain authoritative.

Ungrouped pre-1.0 dependency pin updates remain human-reviewed in a branch distinct from stable pins. The JSONata guard preserves earlier narrower groups, and later package-specific grouping rules remain authoritative.

The TEMPLATE-RENDERED consumer workflows (Rubio-Enterprises/standards -> template/.github/workflows/*.jinja); their action pins (actions/checkout, astral-sh/setup-uv, jdx/mise-action, amannn/action-semantic-pull-request, pnpm/action-setup, ...) are TEMPLATE-OWNED. A per-consumer github-actions bump there just thrashes: Renovate bumps the pin up, then the next template re-render restores the template's own value and the bump is undone. Same thrash the disabled mise manager above fixes for .mise.toml. So disable the github-actions manager for these rendered files fleet-wide; these pins advance with a standards template release instead, reaching consumers through the re-render PRs opened by the native copier manager below (KEEP LAST rule). The re-enable rule below keeps the ONE exception live. cloud-setup-smoke.yml joined this list when it was added as a rendered caller (standards#463): it carries only the first-party pin today, so the disable is a no-op for it right now and exists so a third-party action added to it later is covered by default rather than by remembering to come back here.

Exception to the disable above: the Rubio-Enterprises/.github reusable-workflow `uses:` digests in the rendered workflows ARE meant to advance via Renovate -- that is the `# vN` SHA-pin contract (helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests owns and forward-moves the SHA; this is path C of the standards propagation model). Re-enable + automerge just that dep so a `.github` release still reaches consumers hands-off. minimumReleaseAge:0 exempts this FIRST-PARTY reusable from the global 7-day supply-chain soak: that soak guards against just-published THIRD-PARTY versions, but the org publishes its own `.github` releases deliberately (release-please), so there is nothing to vet -- without this, every `# vN` digest bump sits on `renovate/stability-days` for 7 days before automerging, stalling path C fleet-wide. Must come AFTER the disable rule (later rules win). groupName isolates this dep in its OWN branch: without it, consumer-side github-actions grouping bundles the first-party digest with third-party bumps, and the GROUP then waits on the third parties' 7-day stability — observed on vibetunnel#128, where the urgent lint-hooks credential-fix pin sat behind renovate/stability-days during the v1.55.2 wave. cloud-setup-smoke.yml must be listed here for the same reason standards.yml is: without it the rendered caller's first-party digest falls through to the general github-actions group and waits out the 7-day soak it is explicitly exempt from, which is the whole point of path C being hands-off.

Hand-authored TestFlight callers pinning the Rubio-Enterprises/.github reusable release workflow. Unlike the standards.yml digest above, this target is shared WRITE-CAPABLE release logic: it carries App Store Connect and Match credentials, mutates App Store Connect state, and runs on the persistent signing runner -- a regression reaches Apple, not just a red check. automerge:false forces every advance through a reviewed consumer commit, and the dedicated groupName keeps it out of the general github-actions group so it can never ride in on an unrelated bump. Must come AFTER the first-party reusable rule above (later rules win), which would otherwise automerge it.

Runtime dependency updates that change a shipped tool (`rubio-cli-kit` or `typer`) must use `fix(deps)` so release-please cuts a patch release. This rule changes commit semantics only; the separate fast-lane rule below preserves the standing manual posture for major and 0.x updates.

Group related tool runtime dependencies even when Typer is 0.x. A kit release can raise its Typer floor; separate branches make uv lock fail before either PR exists. This rule controls grouping and the age exemption only. Automerge remains per-upgrade, so a group containing a 0.x Typer update stays manual because Renovate automerges a branch only when every upgrade is automerge-enabled.

Stable non-major tool runtime dependencies use the first-party fast lane: skip the third-party 7-day soak and hand the merge to GitHub as soon as every required check passes. Grouping is separate above so a coupled 0.x Typer floor update remains solvable without widening automerge. Major and 0.x updates remain manual.

Git-sourced uv-tools entries must resolve readable tags to immutable commit SHAs. This narrow rule owns pinDigests because it is a package option, not a custom-manager field; keeping it independent of update type and current version lets Renovate bootstrap a tag-only entry before it can classify the resulting pinDigest update.

Git-sourced tool pins in `home/.chezmoidata/uv-tools.toml` are authoritative first-party fleet inputs. Group stable non-major tag/SHA advances into one PR, skip the org release-age soak, and use scoped platform auto-merge; major and 0.x tool releases stay manual.

Tailscale apt registry for the `deb` datasource. The `customManagers:dockerfileVersions` preset (see extends) reads the `# renovate: datasource=deb depName=tailscale` marker above `ARG TAILSCALE_VERSION` in agent-workspaces' image/Dockerfile, but Renovate's deb datasource has NO default registry: with no registryUrl the lookup returns null and the pin silently never advances. Verified against renovate 43.288.0 (the major renovatebot/github-action@v46.1.14 defaults to, which is what .github-private's runner uses): getPkgReleases({datasource:'deb',packageName:'tailscale'}) returns null, and with the URL below returns 148 releases, newest 1.102.2. `suite=trixie` is COUPLED to the consumer's base image (node:22-trixie-slim) — a consumer on another Debian suite would be offered versions its own apt repo does not serve, so it needs a path-scoped override rather than this rule. binaryArch=amd64 is arbitrary but safe: Tailscale ships an identical version set per arch and the image is built amd64 + arm64 from this one pin. The durable fix is a `registryUrl=` field on the Dockerfile's own `# renovate:` comment line, which keeps the suite beside the FROM line that determines it; that is a change to the consumer repo and is tracked there. Scoped to the custom.regex manager and Dockerfile-shaped files so nothing else can inherit a trixie-specific registry on package identity alone: only the annotated Dockerfile pin this rule was written for picks it up, and any other `deb` + `tailscale` dep keeps Renovate's default (no registry, hence no updates) rather than silently resolving against the wrong Debian suite.

Claude Code tracks the npm `stable` dist-tag rather than `latest`. followTag pins the package to whatever that tag points at (observed 2026-08-17: stable=2.1.226 while latest=2.1.234, i.e. `latest` runs several releases ahead of what Anthropic marks stable), which is the posture we want for an image thousands of agent hours run inside. Two consequences are deliberate. (1) Renovate's docs state that a followTag pin skips the normal major/minor/patch upgrade logic and the stability-days check, so matchUpdateTypes-based gating — including the standing automerge rule above and the global 7-day minimumReleaseAge — cannot be relied on to hold it back. Automerge is therefore all-or-nothing for this package, and we choose ON: the `stable` tag IS the vendor's own soak, so re-soaking it here would only mean running a knowingly older agent. (2) The weekly schedule collapses roughly three stable bumps into a single PR instead of opening one per release; combined with commitMessageTopic it keeps the image's update stream legible in the changelog. Scoped to the custom.regex manager and Dockerfile-shaped files: `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` is an ordinary npm package, so without these selectors any repo that took it as a normal package.json dependency would silently inherit the stable-tag pin, the weekly schedule and the automerge posture — all of which are image-specific decisions, not opinions about the package.

agent-sandbox is consumed as TWO deps that must move as ONE: the Flux GitRepository tag carries the CRDs and manifests (github-tags), and the Flux Kustomization spec.images entry pins the controller image (docker). Renovate would otherwise open a PR per dep, and a split bump briefly runs new CRDs against an old controller — the crash mode reported upstream as kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox#844 — so groupName forces one branch carrying both. Human-merge only: agent-sandbox is pre-1.0 and its CRDs are applied by Flux rather than Helm-upgraded, so a bump can carry a hand-driven v1beta1 -> v1 migration and the release notes have to be read first. The standing safe rule now excludes both plain and v-prefixed 0.x values with `!/^v?0/`; this later explicit override remains as defense in depth for the coupled migration-sensitive class. minimumGroupSize:2 holds the branch back until BOTH deps have an update, so a lone sibling can never open a singleton PR that lands the CRDs without the controller (verified wired at renovate 43.288.0: getMinimumGroupSize in updates/generate.js takes the max across a branch's upgrades, and update/branch/index.js returns `minimum-group-size-not-met` when upgrades.length is short — it skips only branch CREATION, so an existing branch is never retro-cancelled and a Dependency Dashboard tick still forces one through).

mise CLI version pin (the `version:` input on jdx/mise-action across the reusable workflows). Renovate can extract this pin through either the built-in github-actions `uses-with` path or the jdx/mise customManager below, so this dep-name override is deliberately manager-independent. Human-merge only: a broken upstream mise release (e.g. v2026.6.7 shipped without linux-x64 binaries) must be reviewed before the fleet adopts it. The 7-day minimumReleaseAge already blocks same-day releases from automerging; this keeps the final merge a deliberate human decision and overrides the blanket automerge rule above.

uv CLI version pin (the `version:` input on astral-sh/setup-uv across the reusable workflows, tracked by the astral-sh/uv customManager below). Same human-merge posture as the mise CLI pin above, for the same reason: setup-uv runs BEFORE every linter/test in every Python-touching gate, so a bad uv release fails the fleet's gates at a step where no consumer diagnostic has run yet. uv is still 0.x, so the blanket automerge rule's `matchCurrentVersion: !/^v?0/` excludes it today; this explicit override keeps the pin manual after uv reaches 1.0.

customManagers.description: uv CLI pin on astral-sh/setup-uv's `version:` input. Mirrors the jdx/mise manager above; no extractVersionTemplate because astral-sh/uv tags are bare semver (`0.12.1`), not v-prefixed like mise's.

Git-sourced uv-tools entries use recursive matching: the outer expression binds one TOML table to its GitHub repo, and the inner expression replaces only that table's `version` line. The paired package rule enables `pinDigests` so tag-only entries bootstrap, and the explicit replacement always writes the immutable SHA plus readable tag (`version = "<sha>"  # vX.Y.Z`).

Claude Code installed straight into a Dockerfile `RUN npm install -g` line, under the conventional `# renovate:` annotation. The `customManagers:dockerfileVersions` preset in extends only reads `ENV`/`ARG <NAME>_VERSION` assignments, so it cannot see a version embedded in the install command itself; agent-workspaces moved this install under `USER dev` with an NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX, dropping the ARG indirection, which is what makes this manager necessary. Anchoring on the annotation (rather than on `npm install -g` alone) keeps the manager inert on every unannotated global install in the fleet, and requiring currentValue to start with a digit keeps it from capturing a `${VAR}` substitution if a consumer ever reintroduces one — in which case the ARG form is matched by the preset instead, so the two can never both claim the same line. The `stable` dist-tag posture for this dep is the packageRule above.

Private first-party agent-workspace image pins in the agent-workspaces consumer's workspaces manifests. managerFilePatterns treats an entry as a glob unless it is slash-wrapped as a regex, so this pattern is /…/-wrapped; copying it bare into a fileMatch sibling would instead make the slashes literal and match nothing. The tracked value is the branch tag main because the consumer has no releases, so digest updates are the only possible update type.
